Simulation check of negative-binomial count regression (e.g. for RNA-seq /
miRNA counts) parameterised by mean and overdispersion
(`NegativeBinomial2`), comparing an ARD prior (`nb_regression_ard`) with
vague Normal priors (`negbin_regression`). Models in `src/models.jl`.

Source: negative-binomial part of `met_classification/bayesian_stuff.jl`
(the looped `NegativeBinomialRegression` and vectorised `negbinreg` were the
same model; only the vectorised one is kept).

```{julia}
using ExposomicsJulia
using LinearAlgebra, Distributions, Statistics, StatsBase, Random
using Turing, ReverseDiff
```

Simulated data: 200 observations, 5 predictors, `ϕ = 0.82`.

```{julia}
Random.seed!(1234)
X = rand(Normal(0.0, 0.8), 200, 5)
betas = [0.3, -0.5, 1.2, 0.5, -1.1]
m_sim = exp.(1.5 .+ X * betas)
phi_sim = 0.82
y = [rand(NegativeBinomial2(m_sim[i], phi_sim)) for i in 1:200];
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
sampler = NUTS(; adtype = AutoReverseDiff(; compile = true))
chain_ard = sample(nb_regression_ard(X, y), sampler, 5000);
chain_nb  = sample(negbin_regression(X, y), sampler, 5000);
```

Posterior means of the slopes vs the truth:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
hcat(posterior_mean(chain_ard, :β₁), posterior_mean(chain_nb, :β), betas)
```
